title: Epidemiology of Escherichia coli Bacteremia: A Systematic Literature Review

claims.text: E. coli is the most common cause of bacteremia in high-income countries, exceeding other leading bacteremia pathogens including Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pneumoniae.
claims.byte_quote: Escherichia coli is the most common cause of bacteremia in high-income countries, exceeding other leading bacteremia-causing pathogens such as Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pneumoniae

claims.text: E. coli accounted for 27.1% of all bacteremia episodes overall.
claims.byte_quote: The E. coli–specific proportion of all bacteremia episodes was 27.1% overall (95% CI, 24.5–29.8)

claims.text: E. coli proportion of bacteremia varied by acquisition setting: hospital-acquired 18.1%, community-onset healthcare-associated 31.5%, community-acquired 33.0%.
Incidence of E. coli bacteremia rises steeply with age: >100 per 100,000 person-years in 55-to-75-year-olds and >300 in 75-to-85-year-olds.
claims.byte_quote: rates per 100 000 person-years were >100 in 55-to-75-year-olds and >300 in 75-to-85-year-olds

claims.text: Highest relative risks of E. coli bacteremia vs general population: renal dialysis (RR 26.9), solid-organ transplant (RR 20.3), neoplastic disease (RR 14.9).
claims.byte_quote: highest relative risks (RRs) of developing E. coli bacteremia compared with the general population were associated with renal dialysis (RR, 26.9), solid-organ transplantation (RR, 20.3), and neoplastic disease (RR, 14.9)

claims.text: Indwelling vascular and urinary catheters raise E. coli bacteremia risk: central venous 10-fold, peripheral venous 7.5-fold, suprapubic urinary 6-fold, urethral urinary 3-fold.
claims.byte_quote: indwelling vascular and urinary catheters increased the risk...by 10-fold and 7.5-fold for central and peripheral venous catheters, respectively, and by 6-fold and 3-fold for suprapubic and urethral urinary catheters

claims.text: Urinary tract infection was the primary source for 53% of E. coli bacteremia episodes.
claims.byte_quote: Urinary tract infection (UTI) was the primary source for 53% of episodes.

claims.text: Urogenital infection accounted for more than half (pooled 52.6%) of all E. coli bacteremia episodes.
claims.byte_quote: Urogenital infection accounted for more than half of all E. coli bacteremia episodes (pooled estimate, 52.6%; 95% CI, 47.0–58.1%)

claims.text: Pooled case fatality rate for E. coli bacteremia was 12.4%.
claims.byte_quote: The pooled estimated CFR for E. coli bacteremia was 12.4% (95% CI, 10.7–14.3%; range, 2.8–28.5%)
